transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

This is often caused by the container not being pushed all the way home, which tricks the sensor into thinking it's full even when empty. Please slide the water container out completely, check that any small float inside moves freely (not stuck down), and then push it back in firmly until you hear a click. Let me know if it was loose before or if the light stays on after reseating.
Reseated it, it clicks in firmly. I couldn't see a float in there, just a filter/sieve thing which was slimy so I cleaned it. Not sure if the light will stay off yet, will it be fine now?
To work out what to do next, please run a normal drying programme for about 15 minutes and check underneath the machine. Is it leaking water onto the floor, or is the area completely dry?
I haven't run it yet. I can't really see underneath anyway as it's stacked on the washer. Do you want me to run it and just see if the light comes on again?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, please run a normal drying programme for about 20 minutes. Since you cannot check underneath due to stacking, we need to see how it behaves during operation. After it stops, check if the clothes are damp or dry, and look inside the drum to see if any water has collected at the bottom (you can tilt the machine slightly to look). This will tell us if the pump is failing to move water up to the container, which is the most common cause when the light stays on despite an empty tank.

I ran it and it stopped again with the water container light on, even though the container is still nearly empty. The clothes were warm but only partly dry. I can't tilt it because it's stacked on the washer with the tower kit, and I'm not sure what I'd be looking for in the drum. What next?

The machine is likely producing water but failing to move it into the container. This usually means either the condensate pump has failed or its intake is blocked by fluff/sludge (which matches your earlier 'slimy' filter observation). As you can't check underneath, we need to ensure the condenser and sump are clear. Please open the flap at the bottom front, remove the condenser grille, rinse it clean, and check the sump area for any blockage. Let me know if it was clogged or if the sump intake looked clear.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]

I cleaned the condenser and fluff filters, they were fairly clean. I found a small cover near the condenser with some grey slimy water and fluff behind it and wiped what I could reach. Ran it again and it went about 60 minutes this time but the light came on again. What now?

Since the machine ran for 60 minutes but still stopped with an empty tank and damp clothes, the water is being condensed but isn't reaching the container. As you can't see underneath, we need to ensure that bottom access point is clear. Please unplug the machine and check that small cover area again: soak up any water left in the tray and gently clear out the drain hole with a pipe cleaner or brush to remove any hidden fluff blockage.

I already wiped out what I could reach behind that cover, and I'm not sure which bit is the drain hole. I can't get at the back or move the dryer at all because of the tower kit. Is there anything else I can do from the front?

Yes, you can do one more check from the front. The blockage is likely in the small drain hose that carries water from the sump to the pump. This hose sits right inside the compartment where the water container slides out. Please unplug the dryer, remove the container, and look into the hole at the bottom of that cavity. You should see a small rubber tube or pipe; check if it is blocked with fluff or slime. If you can't find one or it's clear, we'll likely need an engineer to access the pump from underneath.

I took the container out and looked in the cavity but honestly I can't tell what I'm looking at, nothing obvious like a rubber tube that I can see. Is it worth getting an engineer in, since I can't reach the back or move it?

Yes, it is time to call an engineer. The symptoms—damp clothes and the light staying on despite an empty tank after 60 minutes of running—indicate that water is being condensed but not pumped out. And cannot access the underside or rear to check the pump or internal hoses due to the stacked installation, this requires a professional diagnosis and likely a pump replacement.

candidates: Water container not seated correctly or float stuck (high)
Faulty condensate pump or float switch (low)
